key_concepts: Greater applied force increases an object's velocity
Lesser applied force results in lower velocity
Inertia is an object's resistance to change in motion
Objects with greater mass have greater inertia
Momentum is the product of mass and velocity
Mass and velocity are the factors that determine momentum
Heavier objects have greater momentum at the same velocity
Faster objects have greater momentum at the same mass
Momentum affects the impact and outcomes of collisions
Adding mass to a moving object increases its effect on objects it hits
Change in momentum occurs during collisions and bounces
Surface characteristics affect collision outcomes such as bounce
